summary: Verified new CSV Lead Import feature end-to-end (backend + frontend). Backend: 10/10 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_csv_leads_import.py covering auth, semicolon-delimited German-column parsing (E-Mail/Vorname/Nachname/Telefonnummer), duplicate detection, response shape ({imported, skipped, errors, total_rows}), source label persistence, phone '+' normalization, non-.csv rejection, and missing-email-column handling. Confirmed 53 leads with source='Facebook Campaign' present in the DB. Frontend: import modal (import-leads-btn → import-leads-modal) opens correctly after login, all three fields (import-file-input, import-label-input default='Facebook Campaign', import-submit-btn) render, uploading a fresh 2-row semicolon CSV via UI produced 'Leads importiert' with count=2 in import-result. Cleaned up 2 TEST_ leads after run.

minor.issue: Non-.csv extension check uses str.endswith('.csv') on file.filename — a file named 'foo.CSV' (uppercase) or missing extension will be rejected. Consider `filename.lower().endswith('.csv')` or MIME-type check for robustness.

Delimiter auto-detect heuristic is fragile: it only switches to ';' if there are ≤2 comma-fieldnames AND the first field contains ';'. A single-column comma CSV whose header itself has a stray semicolon could false-positive. csv.Sniffer would be safer.
Phone normalization blindly prepends '+' if the value doesn't start with '+'. If CSV already contains '00491701...' or a national format, it becomes '+00491701...' which is not a valid E.164 number.

Duplicate check is a single find_one per row inside an async loop — for large CSVs this is N+1. A bulk pre-check (find({'email': {'$in': emails}}) once) would scale better and could dedup within the file itself as well.
No unique index on leads.email → two concurrent imports of the same address can race past the find_one check and create duplicates. Add a MongoDB unique index on `email`.

issues: Recharts throws repeated console warnings 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on initial mount. Non-blocking but noisy — ResponsiveContainer parents likely need a minHeight/minWidth.

Clicking the dimmed backdrop closes the modal AND discards any in-progress import selection — a stray click while a file is chosen wipes the state. Consider requiring an explicit close via the X button when a file is selected.

action_items: Optional: harden .csv extension check to be case-insensitive.
Optional: replace ad-hoc delimiter heuristic with csv.Sniffer.
Optional: guard phone '+' prefix — don't add if value starts with '00' or is empty-after-strip.
Optional: add MongoDB unique index on leads.email to prevent race-condition dupes.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/analytics.py import_leads_csv(): the response includes `total_rows = imported + skipped + len(errors)` — this equals the number of rows PROCESSED, but a caller might reasonably expect it to equal the number of rows in the file (which could be different if the reader chokes mid-file). Consider renaming or documenting.

The FIELD_MAP is case-insensitive via col.strip().lower() but German umlauts in headers (e.g. 'Sekundäre Telefonnummer') rely on exact spelling — a variant like 'Sekundaere' won't map. Fine for the current Facebook export but worth documenting.

The imported lead document sets `name` to `email.split('@')[0]` when Vorname/Nachname/Name are all empty — a reasonable fallback but users importing anonymous email-only lists get pseudo-names like 'john.doe' in the UI.
AnalyticsDashboard.jsx importCSV(): no client-side validation of file size or row count — a user could accidentally upload a 100MB CSV and hang the UI + backend. Add basic size guard.

AnalyticsDashboard.jsx: on successful import, `importResult` remains in state indefinitely (only cleared when the modal reopens via setImportResult(null)); the modal's 'Leads importiert' banner will re-appear stale if the user closes the modal via ESC/backdrop and reopens without going through the button handler. Currently the import-leads-btn onClick does reset it — OK, but backdrop-close does not.

The dashboard component is 1131 lines in a single file, well over the recommended 700-line ceiling. Consider extracting LeadDetailModal, ImportModal, LeadsTable, and UTMLinkGenerator into separate files.

AnalyticsDashboard.jsx exportLeadsCSV() hard-codes credentials `btoa('admin:euroadria2025')` instead of using the passed-in `credentials` prop like every other call in the file. Copy-paste artifact — should be `btoa(\`${credentials.username}:${credentials.password}\`)`.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — import modal opens, all fields render, upload of fresh CSV shows '2 Leads importiert' in import-result

test_credentials: Admin (verified): admin / euroadria2025 via HTTP Basic; also used for admin-login-button in UI.
seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_csvimport_* (backend, 3 rows) and TEST_ui_* (frontend, 2 rows) leads and cleaned them up after the run. 53 pre-existing 'Facebook Campaign' leads left intact.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie consent localStorage key is `euroadria_cookie_consent` (JSON with keys necessary/analytics/marketing/timestamp) — must be pre-seeded BEFORE navigating or the banner overlays the import modal at the bottom of the analytics dashboard and blocks clicks. Facebook Campaign leads are exposed via GET /api/admin/leads (each with source='Facebook Campaign' and imported=true). Test file is in /app/backend/tests/test_csv_leads_import.py — reusable for regression. When creating test CSVs, remember the backend lower-cases emails at insert time, so lookups in GET results must be case-insensitive. Admin exportLeadsCSV in AnalyticsDashboard.jsx hardcodes credentials — flagged as code-review comment.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature addition test, not a bug fix. All 7 required capabilities from the review request verified working: (1) POST /api/admin/leads/import accepts multipart file + source_label; (2) semicolon delimiter auto-detected with German columns mapped via FIELD_MAP; (3) duplicate emails skipped (re-import test returns imported=0, skipped=3); (4) GET /api/admin/leads returns Facebook Campaign leads (≥53 confirmed); (5) import-leads-btn opens import-leads-modal; (6) import-file-input / import-label-input / import-submit-btn all render and work; (7) import-result shows imported count after success.
